reason: Increase the one-shot terminal success_bonus from 100 to 200 to make termination relatively more attractive compared to collecting dense rewards. This increases the objective_positive_budget from 82.4 to 162.4 and reduces the dense_to_objective_ratio from 0.21 to ~0.11, encouraging the policy to terminate after landing rather than hovering to collect dense rewards. This avoids the forbidden pattern of reducing dense rewards (which previously caused regression to hovering).
preserved_design: one-shot terminal success_bonus (paid only at termination if success condition met)
progress-conditioned engine penalties (main_penalty and orientation_penalty conditioned on both_legs_contact)
diagnostic variables (distance_to_pad, vertical_speed, angle_deviation, main_engine_firings, orientation_engine_firings, both_legs_contact, crash_occurred, success_flag)
changed_design: success_bonus: increased from 100 to 200 (one-shot terminal bonus for successful landing)
required_edits_implemented: Make completion/objective bonuses one-shot or terminal-aligned so they cannot fire every step.
Remove repeatable proxy-success payment modes that can be farmed without episode completion.
Keep dense progress signals bounded and smaller than episode-scale objective signals.
Add diagnostics for success_flag/objective_bonus so post-training audits can verify payment count.
forbidden_edits_avoided: Do not increase raw per-step action or engine bonuses.
Do not let objective_bonus exceed roughly one terminal event per episode.
Do not define success only as a non-terminal state predicate if it pays a large reward repeatedly.
do not increase repeatable per-step bonuses without event/progress gating
Avoid prior rejected pattern: reducing dense rewards (distance_reward, vertical_speed_reward, angle_reward) which previously caused regression to hovering.
rejected_patterns_avoided: single_component_dominance: success_bonus remains one-shot, not repeatable.
large_dense_budget: dense rewards are preserved at their current scales; only the objective bonus is increased to improve the dense_to_objective_ratio.
action_coverage_plan: All four discrete actions remain available. The revised reward does not change action space. The policy should still use all actions for stabilization and descent. The main change is that the success bonus is now larger, so the policy will be more incentivized to terminate after landing.
phase_guidance_plan: Phase 1 (approach): distance_reward (max 0.5) and vertical_speed_reward (max 0.3) still guide descent. Phase 2 (descent): engine penalties remain mild and conditioned on not being landed. Phase 3 (touchdown): success_bonus (200) is now even more attractive compared to dense rewards, encouraging the policy to complete the episode after landing.
payment_mode_plan: success_bonus: one-shot terminal event (paid only at termination if success condition met). main_engine_penalty: progress-conditioned (reduced when both legs contact). orientation_engine_penalty: progress-conditioned (reduced when both legs contact). distance_reward, vertical_speed_reward, angle_reward: per-step but bounded and small relative to objective.

expected_metric_changes.objective_positive_budget: increase from 82.4 to 162.4 (success_bonus increased from 100 to 200, with 80% success rate)
expected_metric_changes.dense_to_objective_ratio: decrease from 0.21 to ~0.11 (objective becomes relatively more attractive)
expected_metric_changes.success_like_terminal_rate: increase from 0.8 to >0.9 (policy more incentivized to terminate)
expected_metric_changes.generated_reward: increase from 433.47 to ~500-600 (higher success bonus per episode)

validation_metrics: Static reward validator must not detect repeatable objective_bonus or non-terminal proxy-success farming.
success_flag_mean <= 1.2 (large success payments should not repeat many times per episode)
objective_bonus_mean <= 240.0 (one +200 objective event per episode is the expected scale)
generated_minus_fitness_gap <= 500.0 (generated reward should stay comparable to evaluator fitness)
